title_en: 连成贤诉臧树林排除妨害纠纷案
ruling_gist_en: After signing a house sales contract, the seller shall perform dual delivery of title and physical possession to the buyer. When the buyer has obtained the property title but has not actually occupied the house, if the buyer demands, based solely on a real right claim, that a lawful possessor vacate the premises, the court should carefully examine the matter. If the possessor's occupation of the house is lawful and legitimate, the buyer should file an action for performance of obligation (a claim based on creditor's right) against the counterparty to the contract, demanding the counterparty to perform the obligation to deliver the house, or to bear corresponding liability for breach of contract if the house is objectively unable to be delivered.
keywords_en: Civil; Dispute over removal of nuisance; Dispute over house sales contract; Second-instance trial; Intermediate People's Court; Shanghai; Natural person; General Principles of the Civil Law; Whether a buyer can demand the actual possessor to vacate when ownership and possession right are separated; Application of real right claim and creditor's right claim; Reversal of judgment; House sale; Unauthorized disposition; Property registration; Actual possession; Sales contract; Real right; Cheng Xian v. Zang Shulin — dispute over removal of nuisance
full_text_en:
Lian Chengxian v. Zang Shulin — dispute over removal of nuisance

[Ruling Summary]

After entering into a contract for the sale of a house, the seller shall deliver both the title and the physical possession to the buyer. Where the buyer has obtained the property title but has not yet taken actual possession, the court should carefully examine whether the buyer may demand the eviction of a lawful occupant solely based on a claim of real right. If the occupant's possession of the house is lawful and legitimate, the buyer should file an action for creditor's rights against the other party to the contract, requiring the latter to perform the obligation of delivering the house, or, if the house cannot be physically delivered, to bear corresponding liability for breach of contract.

Plaintiff: Lian Chengxian, male, 30 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Pudong New Area, Shanghai.

Defendant: Zang Shulin, male, 45 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Pudong New Area, Shanghai.

Plaintiff Lian Chengxian filed a lawsuit with the Shanghai Pudong New Area People's Court against Defendant Zang Shulin for a dispute over removal of nuisance.

Plaintiff Lian Chengxian alleged: In 2011, the plaintiff purchased from an outsider, Xie Weizhong, the house located at Room XX, Lane X, Rui'an Road, Zhoupu Town, Pudong New Area, Shanghai. The outsider Xie Weizhong had never performed the obligation of delivering the house. Therefore, on July 5, 2012, the plaintiff filed a lawsuit with the court requesting Xie Weizhong to deliver the house. During the trial, the court added Defendant Zang Shulin as a participant in the proceedings. The defendant claimed that the house sale contract between the plaintiff and Xie Weizhong was void, but this claim was not sustained. The plaintiff has lawfully obtained the title to the disputed house. The defendant still resides in the disputed house, which seriously infringes upon the plaintiff's right to exercise normal property rights as a real right holder. Therefore, the plaintiff requests the defendant to immediately vacate the house located at Room XX, Lane X, Rui'an Road, Zhoupu Town, Pudong New Area, Shanghai.

Plaintiff Lian Chengxian submitted the following evidence in support of his claims:

(1) A copy of the civil judgment (2012) Pu Min Yi (Min) Chu Zi No. 21647, provided to prove that the court ruled the disputed house belongs to the plaintiff.

(2) A copy of the Shanghai Real Estate Register, provided to prove that the property right of the disputed house is registered under the plaintiff.

Defendant Zang Shulin argued: The house located at Room XX, Lane X, Rui'an Road, Zhoupu Town, Pudong New Area, Shanghai belongs to the defendant. The defendant did not sell the disputed house. The sales relationship between the defendant and the outsider Xie Weizhong is void. Therefore, the defendant disagrees with plaintiff Lian Chengxian's claim.

Upon cross-examination at trial, Defendant Zang Shulin had no objection to the authenticity of the evidence provided by Plaintiff Lian Chengxian.

The Shanghai Pudong New Area People's Court found at the first instance:

The house located at Room XX, Lane X, Rui'an Road, Zhoupu Town, Pudong New Area, Shanghai was originally purchased by Defendant Zang Shulin with compensation and resettlement funds after his house was demolished. In August 2008, the title of the disputed house was registered in the defendant's name. The house was occupied and used by the defendant and his family. On August 12, 2011, an outsider, Li Zhen, acting as the defendant's agent, entered into a "Shanghai Real Estate Sales Contract" with another outsider, Xie Weizhong, for the disputed house, stipulating a transfer price of RMB 800,000. On August 12, 2011, a real estate transfer registration application was submitted to the relevant authorities. Subsequently, the title of the disputed house was registered under the name of Xie Weizhong. In October 2011, Plaintiff Lian Chengxian and the outsider Xie Weizhong entered into a sales contract for the house located at Room XX, Lane X, Rui'an Road, Zhoupu Town, Pudong New Area, Shanghai, stipulating a transfer price of RMB 1,100,000. On April 5, 2012, the title of the disputed house was registered under the plaintiff's name. On July 5, 2012, the plaintiff sued Xie Weizhong, requesting delivery of the disputed house. The defendant applied to participate in the proceedings as a third party. The court later ruled: declaring void the "Shanghai Real Estate Sales Contract" executed in the defendant's name with the outsider Xie Weizhong for the disputed house; dismissing the plaintiff's claim for Xie Weizhong to deliver the disputed house; and dismissing the defendant's claim to declare void the sales relationship between the plaintiff and Xie Weizhong concerning the disputed house. The plaintiff, claiming that he had lawfully obtained the disputed house and that the defendant's continued residence there seriously infringed upon his right to exercise property rights as a real right holder, filed this lawsuit, requesting the defendant to immediately vacate the house located at Room XX, Lane X, Rui'an Road, Zhoupu Town, Pudong New Area, Shanghai.

The Shanghai Pudong New Area People's Court held at the first instance:

Property ownership means the right of an owner to possess, use, dispose of, and enjoy the fruits of his property in accordance with law. Anyone who encroaches upon state, collective, or another's property shall return the property, and if return is impossible, the value shall be compensated. In this case, based on the evidence provided by Plaintiff Lian Chengxian, it is sufficient to prove that the plaintiff is the lawful owner of the house located at Room XX, Lane X, Rui'an Road, Zhoupu Town, Pudong New Area, Shanghai, and is entitled to the rights of possession, use, disposal, and enjoyment of fruits in accordance with law. Defendant Zang Shulin is no longer the property owner of the above house and has no right to occupy or use the house. Therefore, the plaintiff's request for the defendant to vacate the house should be granted. However, given the actual circumstances of this case, the defendant should be given a certain period of time to find alternative housing. The defendant's arguments that the disputed house belongs to him and that he did not sell it are inconsistent with the facts and lack legal basis; the court does not adopt them.

In summary, in accordance with Article 117, paragraph 1, of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, the Shanghai Pudong New Area People's Court rendered the following judgment on December 23, 2013:

Defendant Zang Shulin shall vacate the house located at Room XX, Lane X, Rui'an Road, Zhoupu Town, Pudong New Area, Shanghai within two months from the effective date of this judgment.

Zang Shulin, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, arguing that the appellee Lian Chengxian had colluded with an outsider to fraudulently obtain the title certificate of the disputed house, and that Zang Shulin had ownership of the disputed house. He requested the court of second instance to reverse the judgment and dismiss Lian Chengxian's first-instance claims.

Appellee Lian Chengxian argued that the first-instance judgment was correct and requested the court of second instance to affirm it.

The Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, upon second-instance trial, confirmed the facts found at first instance.

The Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court held at the second instance:

The issue in dispute is: Where ownership and the right of possession are separated, can the buyer, as the owner of the house, demand the eviction of the actual occupant of the house based on a claim for return of property?

First, the effective judgment has confirmed that the sales contract executed in the name of Defendant Zang Shulin by the outsider Li Zhen, as agent, with the outsider Xie Weizhong for the disputed house is void. That is, the first-hand sale was not the true intention of the original owner Zang Shulin, and the contract has no legal effect on Zang Shulin ab initio. Zang Shulin has resided in the disputed house since August 2008 and has possessed and used it lawfully. Therefore, where the property owner Lian Chengxian has never obtained actual control of the house from the seller Xie Weizhong, the court does not support his demand for the direct eviction of the actual occupant Zang Shulin.

Second, in the second-hand sale transaction, Appellee Lian Chengxian and the outsider Xie Weizhong entered into a real estate sales contract for the disputed house and paid corresponding consideration. This sales contract has been confirmed as valid by an effective judgment and is thus legally binding on both Lian Chengxian and Xie Weizhong. Both parties shall perform their respective obligations in accordance with the contract. Therefore, Lian Chengxian's rights in the disputed house should be realized through the performance of the real estate sales contract (including the transfer of title and physical delivery). In this case, although Lian Chengxian obtained the real estate title certificate for the disputed house on April 5, 2012, completing the transfer of title, he has never obtained possession or the right to use the disputed house. For this, Lian Chengxian should, based on the real estate sales contract with Xie Weizhong, assert claims for creditors' rights against the other party to the contract. Considering the circumstances of this case, since the first-hand sales contract has been confirmed void, the outsider Xie Weizhong never lawfully acquired the disputed house and is objectively unable to perform the obligation of delivering the house to Lian Chengxian. Therefore, Lian Chengxian should claim from Xie Weizhong liability for breach of contract due to the inability to deliver the house, resulting in the contract's inability to be further performed.

In summary, in accordance with Article 170, paragraph 1, item (2), of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on March 13, 2014:

1. Revoke the civil judgment (2013) Pu Min Yi (Min) Chu Zi No. 36805 of the Shanghai Pudong New Area People's Court;

2. Dismiss Lian Chengxian's claim requesting Zang Shulin to vacate the house located at Room XX, Lane X, Rui'an Road, Zhoupu Town, Pudong New Area, Shanghai.

This judgment is final.
